summary.text: Trever Nehls is the Republican nominee for this open southwest-Houston-area seat, previously held by his twin brother Troy Nehls. He served two terms as a Fort Bend County constable, is a colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve according to a 2020 news report, and lost races for county sheriff (2020) and county judge (2022). He is running on border enforcement, lower costs, support for law enforcement and infrastructure, according to his campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia.

paragraphs.text: Is the twin brother of Troy Nehls, the district's previous Representative.

Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and corrections from the University of Wisconsin–Platteville, a master's degree in public administration from Central Michigan University, and a master's degree in military strategic studies from the U.S. Army War College.
Was a colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve and was deployed to the Middle East in March 2020, according to ABC13; his campaign website describes him as a former constable and police officer.
Worked in the private sector and founded Nehls Consulting, LLC.
Served two terms as Fort Bend County Precinct 4 constable, from 2013 to 2020.
Won the 2020 Republican primary for Fort Bend County Sheriff with 82 percent of the vote, according to ABC13, and lost the general election to Democrat Eric Fagan, 52.6% to 47.4%.
Was the Republican nominee for Fort Bend County Judge in 2022 and lost to incumbent KP George, 51.6% to 48.4%.
Announced his candidacy for Texas's 22nd District after his brother decided not to seek re-election, and won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 75.7% of the vote over Rebecca Clark.

sources.title: Former Fort Bend County Constable Trever Nehls announces bid for Congress in Texas' 22nd District
Twin of Fort Bend County sheriff Troy Nehls wins GOP primary while deployed overseas
